newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money rates rise to 3.50 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money rates rise to 3.50 pct.

text.p: German call money rates rose on Friday, hitting a high of around four percent before easing back to around 3.50 percent, as the customary scramble to fulfil end-of-month reserve requirements boosted demand.
Dealers said the usual end-of-month pressure had been eased by Thursday's relatively high borrowings at the Lombard window, which totalled some three billion marks.
"That helped to work the rate back down to 3.50 percent," said one dealer.
Deposits at the central bank rose on Thursday to 45.6 billion marks from 44.7 billion.
The monthly average rose to 40.8 billion marks from 40.7 billion.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was at 3.84417 percent on Friday versus 3.19583 percent.
